GC Tech: AI/AR glasses: Point-of-view shots, hands-free communication and AI access offer a new digital option; Raising China TAM
AI/AR glasses provide point-of-view (POV) shots, hands-free communication, and AI access, offering users a new way to connect with the digital world. They make first-person perspective (FPP) photography easier without the need to hold up a smartphone and keep it level; allow hands-free communication via voice command; and offer a direct interface to AI assistance and augmented reality, making the world more interactive. Current AI functions include live caption, real-time translation, visual based Q&A, AR navigation and AI smart assistant. The hands-free human-machine interaction make AI/AR glasses easier to use in daily life, positioning them as a potential successor to smartphones.
The specifications of AI/AR glasses are also being enhanced, with more cameras to capture user motions and to detect the environment, stronger AI foundation models to bring smarter AI assistance, more displays with full colour and higher resolution to enhance interaction, lighter weight to lengthen wearing hours, etc. With more AI/AR glasses launches to come, with better specifications, we raise China AI/AR glasses shipment by 87% / 121% in 2026 / 27E to 3.7m / 7.0m units, and expect it to grow at a 32% CAGR in 2027-30E to 16m units by 2030E. We expect the market size to grow at 132% YoY in 2026E to US\$946m and to grow at 24% CAGR in 2027-30E to US\$3bn by 2030E. Read more: AI/AR glasses China TAM; AI/AR glasses product tracker.
Note: AI glasses are smart glasses with AI features; they usually come with only audio interaction, without display. AR glasses come with a digital overlay of a display on top of the

Use cases and potential buyers
Exhibit 6: First perspective videos to record good memories
Unique first perspective experience. Compared to smart devices, glasses provide a distinct user experience as they offer a first-person perspective. They see what users see, display objects right in front of the eyes, and produce sounds right next to the ears. We believe the first-person perspective is part of the reason why AI/AR glasses have gained popularity on social media, with users able instantly to share what they see with others. Compared to smartphones and tablets that require users to hold up a screen, glasses display information naturally and directly in the line of sight.

- Display message and notification with multipleways
-Allowing user to instantly reply with text or audio

AI/AR glasses can be helpful in both personal life and gaming (Exhibit 7). AI/AR glasses support navigation for walking and biking, presenting directions as overlays. Users can conveniently capture first person photos and video with video commands. The glasses can also display notifications and message replies, providing a hands-free experience. With a large display and surround speakers, they also offer an immersive gaming experience.

AI/AR glasses serve as highly efficient productivity tools (Exhibit 8). With advanced audio processing capabilities, they provide meeting notes/ summaries, real time translation, and automatic presentation scripts. Also with generative AI and web search technologies, AI/AR glasses can support visual-based Q&A (for example, asking the AI for information on an object the user is looking at) and conversation support (automatically showing supporting information for real-time conversations), which can be useful in classes or in sales support scenarios. Lastly, portable AI/AR glasses can provide a virtual workdesk wherever you are.

AI/AR glasses will come with unrestricted usage scenarios (Exhibit 9). Thanks to its light-weight (35-80g in general), AI/AR glasses are portable. They can be used at home for entertainment, at office for work, in flight/ in vehicles/ outdoors. The increased display technology quality, albeit still with room for improvement, ensures display quality in strong/weak light environments. Display technologies are also improving to reduce motion sickness when traveling.
Hands-free experience with smooth audio command and gesture control. AI/AR glass users benefit especially from the hands-free experience. They can pick up phone calls, read and reply to notifications, take photos/ videos, access step by step recipes while cooling, check the weather and calendar, and get navigational directions in real-time. All the above features can be achieved through smart audio control, which intelligently responds to conversational / casual commands powered by LLMs. Some glasses also offer an electromyography (EMG) wristband, which can precisely recognize finger movements such as swiping and tapping. Empowered by these technologies, users find the glasses useful in scenarios such as exercising, while carrying bags, cooking, and when their hands are occupied caring for children.

Specification and AI functions
We expect AI/AR glasses makers will continue to improve the user experience, including through 1) improving battery life, with better materials or more advanced battery management algorithms, 2) increasing the display quality; we believe AI glasses with displays will become the mainstream specification, 3) reducing weight, by changing raw materials and coming up with better system designs, 4) introducing more form factors and more frame options to fit different facial structures, 5) more practical features with AI to expand user scenarios.
AI/AR glasses connect humans and the AI computing network. The popularity of Ray-ban Meta glasses shows that users value simple yet effective features, such as picking up phone calls, listening to music, hand-free photo and video capture, and simple smart Q&A powered by AI, rather than complex AI models. The enhanced user experience and more natural interactions drive AI/AR glasses demand. With the emergence of Gen-AI that provides human-like conversations, consumer behaviors have evolved to integrate the interaction with smart devices as a seamless part of daily life.
Key AI features include (1) live caption with AI summary and AI translation; (2) multi-modal object recognition; (3) music recognition; (4) real-time information search powered by conversational AI; (5) navigation with AR display. At the current stage, AI features serve as the attraction for users to try on the glasses, and we expect more practical AI features to be launched to retain users.
The hardware specification upgrade opportunities include: (1) advanced display, including LCOS, Micro OLED, Micro LED, (2) optics solutions, migrating from Birdbath to waveguide, and potentially SiC based waveguide in 2027, (3) custom SoC for image/ audio low power processing, and (4) new accessories such as rings and wristbands.
Display: AI/AR glasses’ full colour display quality is usually beyond the expectation of first time users. They show clear and vivid display, thanks to the LCOS/ Micro OLED/ Micro LED that are place close to the eyes.

Battery: While the battery life has been improving, it in general can last for less than 10 hours, vs. smart watches that can now last for one day to one week. As an accessory for daily use, it needs to have enough battery strength and fast charging capability.
Weight: Current AI/AR glasses without displays reduce the weight to 35-40g, compared to normal glasses at 10-30g. When first tried on, based on our experience, users find the weight is generally acceptable. But after long-term use, users may feel pressure on their nose and ears. Glasses with display weights of 50-80g still have large room to improve. Also, when carrying glasses, the charging boxes weigh 160g+, and the size is not easy to fit in a pocket either.
Design: AI/AR glasses now look very similar to normal glasses, although the legs and frames are slightly thicker. They come in different colour options for frames, such as red, coffee, grey, violet, and the lens can be clear or transition. Given the similar look to normal glasses, we believe users would feel comfortable wearing them in daily life.

Model reviews
AI/AR glasses are developing rapidly, driving hardware upgrades of the consumer electronics supply chains. Key upgrade trends are across display, optics, SoCs, audio algorithm and smart accessories.
n Display: LCOS (matured, low cost, high brightness, while large size), Micro OLED (outstanding colour but lower brightness) and Micro LED (high brightness, outstanding colour, low power consumption while high cost) are major technologies. Current mainstream options are full colour LCOS (Meta Ray-Ban Display), full colour Micro OLED (RayNeo Air 4 Pro) and green colour Micro LED (Rokid glasses). The industry the still developing full colour Micro LED solutions, which some believe it will be the ultimate solution.
n Optics/ Lens: the current mainstream solution is Birdbath (matured, while large size and low light transmittance), while waveguide (much lighter and thinner, similar to traditional lens) is increasingly popular. Micro OLED are usually paired with birdbath solutions, and LCOS and Micro LED are used with waveguide as they can provide higher brightness. Xreal Project Aura (2026, partnership with Google) will adopt Birdbath, and the recently announced Meta Ray-Ban display comes with Arrayed waveguide. For 2027, the industry is exploring SiC waveguide, which will be thinner, lighter, are more stable in high temperature than traditional solution.
n Low power consumption chips: AI glass suppliers are using various SoC solutions to achieve better power efficiency. For example, Xiaomi AI glasses apply Qualcomm Snapdragon chip for image processing and the Bestechnic chip for audio processing. Media reported that Apple will design a custom chip for its AI glasses in 2027.
n More smart accessories are applied. Rings and wristbands are potential accessories that can work well with AI glasses. Hand gestures, hand/ finger movements can be used as input signals to control glasses. The health data detected by the smart rings/ wristbands can also be integrated into the smart AI assistant. Meta Ray-Ban Display comes with a smart EMG wristband.

AI glasses shipment review
Exhibit 18: Meta AI glasses’ exponential growth Cummulative shipment of Meta’s AI glasses
The first generation of Ray-Ban Stories (launched in 3Q21) sales were around 300-400k units throughout lifetime, as reported by media. The second generation Ray-Ban Meta (launched in 3Q23) glasses gained greater success, with EssilorLuxottica stating that between October 2023 (when Ray-Ban Meta was launched) to Feb 2025 they sold 2million units. We attributed the success to the improved specification including camera (5MP to 12MP, 720P videos to 1080P), memory (4GB to 32GB), better battery life (3hrs to 4hrs), better audio (added directional audio) and more fun features including Meta AI and live streaming on Facebook and Instagram. With stronger AI functions and a more comfortable wearing experience, the supply chain in China remains positive on the AI/AR glasses shipment ramp up in 2026 / 27E at triple digit growth from the low base. The next generation of AR glasses targeting to launch in Sep 2026, embedded with more cameras to capture motion and dual display with better resolution, could drive shipment to surpass 1m vs. the current generation at several hundred thousands units.
To measure the potential size of AI/AR glasses buyers in China, we consider: (1) regular glasses users: Meta’s AI glasses co-branded with Ray-ban have been a success, leveraging the large user base of sunglasses in US and Europe. In Asia, while the usage of sunglasses is less frequent, the region has a higher myopia prevalence rate. According to National Health Commission data (link), China has 660m myopic people in 2020, increased from 540m in 2016, suggesting a large population used to wearing glasses. (2) Acceptance of new technologies: consumers in China appear willing to try new technologies, such as drones, robots, robotaxis, VR headsets, AI/AR glasses, etc, supporting the growth of new tech gadgets.

We raise our China AI/AR glasses volume forecast by 56%\~132% in 2025-30E (Exhibit 19), supported by more model launches and a firmer outlook for the adoption of AI/AR glasses. We expect China’s AI/AR glasses volume to grow at 79% CAGR in 2024-30, reaching 10m shipment by 2028 and 16m shipment by 2030E. Our ASP assumptions are unchanged, still expecting AR glass ASP to decrease to US\$253 by 2030 in China and AI glass ASP to US\$130, which is more affordable for mass market users. With that, we forecasrt China’s AI/AR glasses market to grow at a 61% CAGR to US\$3bn by 2030E. AI features driving adoption. We believe the integration of Llama 3 AI assistant in April 2024 is one of the drivers of Ray-Ban Meta glasses’ success. In the China market, AI and AR glasses already feature advanced hardware specifications; however, the AI experience still has room to improve. We expect China’s supply chains to catch up, given with their solid experience in application development to deliver innovative and user-friendly features for AI/AR glasses. The China market also embraces new technologies, which further supports our expectations for accelerated adoption of AI/AR glasses in the market. Models with displays to be the mainstream. As displaying information is a seamless part of the first-person perspective experience, we expect AI/AR glasses with displays to become the mainstream. While previously Meta’s no-display AI glasses gained popularity, we believe it was an accepted compromise at the time as the display technology still needed time to mature. For the China market, we expect glasses with displays (which we categorize as AR glasses) will see TAM size growth to US\$1.8bn over 13 Goldman Sachs GC Tech December 2025

2023-30E, a larger upside than glasses without displays (which we refer to as AI glasses) where we expect TAM to increase to US\$1.0bn over 2023-30E (Exhibit 20). Exhibit 20: We expect AI/AR glasses with displays to see stronger upside AR/ AI glasses China TAM Higher growth than TWS ramp up in China. We model China AI/AR glasses shipment to grow at a 79% CAGR in 2024-30E, at a higher rate than TWS earbuds at 64% CAGR in 2017-23 during the technology’s initial ramp up (Exhibit 24). We expect a faster pace of growth for AI/AR glasses than TWS earbuds, as they not only serve as a functional tool that improves efficiency, but also as a fashion accessory with many different styles. Moreover, the various AI functions, such as live caption, real-time translation, and AR navigation are useful new features that are likely to attract users.

GS Factor Profile The Goldman Sachs Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows: Growth is based on a stock’s forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock’s forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock’s forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile). Financial Returns and Multiple use the Goldman Sachs analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics). For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative. M&A Rank Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.
